verdict.rationale: Kimi has a well-documented public API: a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1 spec covering chat completions, responses, Anthropic-compatible messages, batches, files and models, plus an Admin API spec, a per-endpoint Try-it playground, and /v1 path versioning. However, the vendor's own probe-verified docs say this API belongs to the separate Kimi API Open Platform, and there is no public API for the kimi.com assistant app itself, so its agent mode, memory, scheduled tasks and PPT features cannot be driven programmatically. Only file Q&A is documented as mirrored. missing for 10: API coverage of the assistant app's own features (agent tasks, memory, scheduling), an API changelog/deprecation policy, independent hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Kimi intelligent assistant can upload files and answer questions based on those files. The Kimi API offers the same functionality.
The Kimi Code API is compatible with both OpenAI and Anthropic protocols.
The Kimi Admin API lets organization administrators manage members, invitations, projects, and inference API keys programmatically, and query billing, usage, and audit logs
Kimi members can create and manage API Keys in the Kimi Code Console
